QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_14

question.text: Per the NISM-Series-VIII workbook, for futures contracts on index or individual securities where next-day mark-to-market settlement value may not be collected before next-day trading begins, the initial margin is computed using a VaR approach with:

answer.text: 99% confidence level and a two-day time horizon
95% confidence level and a one-day time horizon
99% confidence level and a one-day time horizon
95% confidence level and a five-day time horizon

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states initial margin is generally based on 99% VaR over a one-day horizon. For futures contracts on index or individual securities where the next-day MTM settlement value may not be collected before next-day trading begins, a two-day horizon is used in that conditional case. The Trap: The two-day horizon is not a blanket rule for all single-stock derivatives based on volatility; it is a conditional adjustment for the next-day MTM collection scenario described in the source. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), page 161.
